pages.title: What Is Air Quality?
pages.text: The air in SteamCraft is tracked in three ways: $(bold)CO2$(), $(bold)Toxins$(), and $(bold)Microplastics$(). Each one builds up from different sources and causes different problems. The cleaner the air, the healthier you and your world will be.

pages.title: CO2 (Carbon Dioxide)
pages.text: CO2 builds up when you breathe, when mobs are nearby, and when furnaces run. When CO2 gets too high (above 60), you start taking damage. It also kills torches — they go out when there's too much CO2 in the air!

pages.title: Toxins
pages.text: Toxins come from lava, polluted biomes, and industrial processes like smelting. If toxins rise above 40, you'll get poisoned. Toxins also harm your crops, slowing or even killing them.

pages.title: Microplastics
pages.text: Microplastics are tiny plastic particles that build up in the environment. They cause slowness when levels get too high. Unlike CO2 and toxins, microplastics don't decay as quickly — so be careful about how much plastic you use.

pages.title: Good News!
pages.text: Air quality naturally improves over time through decay and ventilation. Trees and leaves absorb CO2. You can speed up recovery with the $(bold)Air Scrubber$(). The Nether, however, is always maximally polluted — wear protection!
